question: What did your family believe about a relative that turned out to be completely wrong?
story: My family spent eleven years convinced my dad had secretly won the lottery and was hiding it from us. It started when he paid cash for a truck. Then he paid off my sister's tuition in one check. He never explained anything, because explaining things was not something my father did. My aunt was certain. She told the entire family he had a winning ticket and a secret account. Relatives we had not seen in years suddenly called on holidays. One cousin asked him for a loan at a funeral. Dad just smiled and said he had gotten lucky. Here is the truth. He never won a thing. He had been couponing like a man possessed since nineteen ninety four, buying groceries for half the street at eighty percent off and quietly investing the difference. We found the binders when he retired. Eleven of them. My aunt still has not forgiven him.
